NariQ: BF16-level Qwen3.8-27B in a 10 GB file
stories.text:
We built NariQ: 3-bit-or-lower quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B that retain near-BF16 quality across agentic tasks, math, multilingual reasoning, and image understanding.

To our knowledge, this is the first 3-bit-or-lower quantization that retains BF16 lvl performance on long-horizon agentic tasks.

Benchmarks (BF16 / 3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit):

- DeepSWE: 39.8 / 41.0 / 41.9 / 28.6

- Terminal-Bench 2.1: 62.6 / 63.8 / 60.2 / 52.4

- AIME 25+26: 97.7 / 98.3 / 96.5 / 86.0

- MSGM: 94.0 / 93.1 / 91.8 / 90.6

- RealWorldQA: 82.4 / 82.4 / 81.3 / 80.9

Decode speed is comparable to other quants on an RTX PRO 6000. Context-length results below

(3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit / Unsloth UD-IQ3_XXS):

- 4K: 88.9 / 99.2 / 111.7 / 94.7

- 16K: 84.5 / 93.8 / 105.1 / 89.8

- 64K: 70.7 / 77.5 / 85.0 / 74.8

Running these currently require our llama.cpp fork: (https://github.com/nari-labs/nari-llama.cpp)

Feedback and questions welcome. We'd love to hear how these perform on your workloads.

Show HN: Hermit CRM – Free open-source CRM for solopreneurs
stories.text:
I was about to keep track of my clients and prospecting in Google Sheets for my solopreneur business, when I remembered that's exactly what I advise my clients not to do.

Created Hermit CRM, an open source CRM for 1 person. Hermit helps to keep track of deals and prospecting. The platform is built for AI by storing the data in Markdown files in git, stored locally and can be accessed with a web app, CLI or MCP. No telemetry on the app. Building in public, even the website stats are public as well.

It’s macOS first. Linux is less tested, and Windows isn’t supported.

Features I'm proud of: - import somebody from LinkedIn into to the CRM with 1 click - adding a LinkedIn convo to the CRM with 1 click. Both work without LinkedIn or CRM subs.

Don't like what you see? Fork the Hermit with your AI.

Would love to learn how you're using Hermit and where it doesn't fit your workflows.

Show HN: News Blocklist – a DNS blocklist of 14k news and current-affairs sites
stories.text:
A little while ago I built (vibed) a tiny Mac app to block websites via the hosts file. By default it imported some fairly popular adult filtering lists as well as social media etc.

It has been very effective; it would only take a few moments to switch off but it is enough of an interruption to often make me re-evaluate and proceed on.

I have a particular distain for current affairs and have found "the news" addictive for years, clearly at the detriment to my own mental health and sanity.

So, in a similar vein to the other lists I found, I have created a fairly comprehensive list of news sites that can be imported/used as you see fit.

To state the obvious, the absolute vast majority of the work was done via Claude and a small army of sub-agents.

Coworker rejects PR (one month in) because it does not meet his standards
stories.text: just joined this new team about 1 year into their development. Demoed the work to the team about two weeks ago (half way in). Work is practically complete & runs well no issues. I create PR & assign the two PR reviewers (one my rank another a rank above me). one colleague (the one at my level) leaves some constructive comments no functional changes. The other colleague (one rank above me) says something equivalent to "does not meet our standards" "do not do x pattern since we have used y (which has a huge limitation)" to use Y pattern I would basically need to change most of the logic and it would be about 70% waste. I demoed my code with this pattern two weeks ago and there were no issues/comments from the team. The code is concise and easy to read. I had a call with the colleague and explained the code and why I used it, and showed him some other parts of the codebase where this pattern should be used, his only defense was that "it does not meet our standards because it uses X rather than y pattern, since we used y pattern in the past, we should only use y pattern" while x pattern is very similar only removing the limitation that was causing the code to be difficult to maintain etc. This "standard requirement" is written nowhere as a hard requirement and the codebase is barely one year old, with only one of the codebase founders still on the team.... I'm going to have a chat with the manager tomorrow morning.

Show HN: Genesis Map – Visualize your agent's changes. See where they can break
stories.text:
When agent ships code faster and faster, human review is no longer possible. Which brings 2 problems, at least for me:

1. I need to understand what my agent changes as quickly and easily as possible, cuz I don't wanna lose track of the current status of my product, or be the main bottleneck in shipping code.

2. I don't trust what my agent tells me. Many times, I've been suffered from agent telling me "all is well", then say "you are right, sorry, I missed..." after code failed on production.

To mitigate those problems, I made Genesis, a skill for coding agent to generate a beautiful flow chart to understand all the business flows, flag all risk changes and untested code between commits. It worked very well on me, so I benchmarked it against vanilla Claude code and Codex:

Vanilla → With Genesis 1. Test gaps caught: Claude Code 8% → 38% · Codex 4% → 23%

2. False alarms per review: Claude Code 2.1 → 0.7 · Codex 1.4 → 0.5

3. Real risks found per review: Claude Code 2.9 → 2.8 · Codex 2.4 → 2.4

Show HN: I used Fable to make an open source 80s-style Skyrim browser game
stories.text:
Inspired by both Skyrim and the old Sierra games like King's Quest

Features:

- Playable in the browser on desktop and mobile

- Play by clicking, tapping, number keys, or typing

- Original code-drawn pixel art and synthesised music

- Day and night, snow, and a thaw

- Real-time combat with timed parries

- Six skills that rise by use, with perks

- Five spells and four runewords

- Trading, a forge, and repeatable paid work

- Weight limit for what you carry, and a storage chest

- Map, journal, character sheet, and deeds list

- Two-part main story with two endings

- Eleven side stories

- Valley with eight fable-made places and interiors

- Endlessly generated open country beyond the valley

- Eighteen fable-written scenes to find in the wild

- Three far landmarks

- Walls of rock with passes guarded by enemies

- Vaults under ruined towers

- Autosave plus three manual slots

- No runtime dependencies

Limitations:

- Story inconsistencies

- Mismatches between story/description and visual state

- I'm sure plenty more
